statement: The function returns an integer r equal to the maximum length of a contiguous substring of s that contains at most two distinct byte values. More explicitly, for indices 0 <= i <= j < len(s), let the substring s[i..j] be s[i], s[i+1], ..., s[j] and let its length be j-i+1. Then r = max { j-i+1 | 0 <= i <= j < len(s) and the set { s[k] | i <= k <= j } has cardinality at most 2 }.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 100000; every byte of s is an English ASCII letter (in 65..90 or 97..122).

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r. In particular, it does not fail, panic, access memory out of bounds, or overflow.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 100000; every byte of s is an English ASCII letter (in 65..90 or 97..122).

statement: The function returns a result r and r <= len(s).
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 100000; every byte of s is an English ASCII letter (in 65..90 or 97..122).

statement: The function returns a result r with r >= 1, and if len(s) >= 2 then r >= 2.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 100000; every byte of s is an English ASCII letter (in 65..90 or 97..122).

statement: If the set of byte values occurring in s has cardinality at most 2, then the function returns r = len(s).
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 100000; every byte of s is an English ASCII letter (in 65..90 or 97..122).

statement: If the set of byte values occurring in s has cardinality greater than 2, then the function returns a result r with r < len(s), equivalently r <= len(s)-1.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 100000; every byte of s is an English ASCII letter (in 65..90 or 97..122).

statement: If len(s) >= 3 and all byte values occurring in s are pairwise distinct, that is s[i] != s[j] for every 0 <= i < j < len(s), then the function returns r = 2.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 100000; every byte of s is an English ASCII letter (in 65..90 or 97..122).

statement: The function returns a result r and there exist indices i and j with 0 <= i <= j < len(s) such that j-i+1 = r and the set { s[k] | i <= k <= j } has cardinality at most 2.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 100000; every byte of s is an English ASCII letter (in 65..90 or 97..122).

statement: The function returns a result r and for every pair of indices i and j with 0 <= i <= j < len(s), if the set { s[k] | i <= k <= j } has cardinality at most 2, then j-i+1 <= r.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 100000; every byte of s is an English ASCII letter (in 65..90 or 97..122).

statement: If the set of byte values occurring in s has cardinality greater than 2, then the function returns a result r and there exist indices i and j with 0 <= i <= j < len(s) such that j-i+1 = r and the set { s[k] | i <= k <= j } has cardinality exactly 2.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 100000; every byte of s is an English ASCII letter (in 65..90 or 97..122).

statement: The function returns a result r for s. For every nonempty contiguous substring t of s, meaning t[k] = s[a+k] for some a with 0 <= a and 1 <= len(t) and a+len(t) <= len(s), if the same function returns r_t on input t, then r_t <= r.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 100000; every byte of s is an English ASCII letter (in 65..90 or 97..122).

statement: The function returns a result r for s. For every byte c such that len(s) < 100000 and c is an English ASCII letter, let s' be the sequence obtained by appending c to s, and let r' be the result returned by the same function on s'. Then r' = r or r' = r+1.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 100000; every byte of s is an English ASCII letter (in 65..90 or 97..122).

statement: Let rev(s) be the sequence of length len(s) defined by rev(s)[i] = s[len(s)-1-i] for all 0 <= i < len(s). If the function returns r on s and r_rev on rev(s), then r_rev = r.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 100000; every byte of s is an English ASCII letter (in 65..90 or 97..122).

statement: Let t be any nonempty byte sequence with len(t) = len(s), len(t) <= 100000, all bytes of t English ASCII letters, and for all 0 <= i,j < len(s), s[i] = s[j] if and only if t[i] = t[j]. If the function returns r on s and r_t on t, then r_t = r.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 100000; every byte of s is an English ASCII letter (in 65..90 or 97..122).
